A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research project, renamed from OmniDRCA to DrVoice, with shared architecture, training data, and retained experiments. All 18 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison; the substantial revision does not create material reading gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original spoken-QA and speech-quality results, component ablations, data-scaling experiments, and full-duplex interruption results in Tables 2–8 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: V2 reports original DrVoice benchmark results, encoder and grouping ablations, pretraining analyses, and GPU-hour measurements in Tables 2–5 and Figures 2–3.

M1.justification: V2 adds a Whisper-Large-v3 continuous speech encoder and adapter alongside grouped discrete tokens, and removes contrastive alignment and its loss (Sections 3.1–3.2). V1's full-duplex TDM extension and assistant-state prediction head are also removed. The grouping/ungrouping mechanism, autoregressive speech refinement, and seven-pattern training mixture persist; SRM-to-SRH and CoM-Mixing terminology alone do not establish additional procedural changes.

E1.justification: Reported QA coverage contracts from AlpacaEval, Web Questions, Llama Questions, and TriviaQA to only Web Questions and Llama Questions. V1's simulated interruption/non-interruption conversation training and multi-turn interruption evaluation disappear with Appendix A. The principal English training sources and seven speech/text interaction patterns remain.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds QA comparisons with Kimi-Audio, Qwen2.5-Omni, Freeze-Omni, MinMo, LLaMA-Omni2, VITA-Audio, Stream-Omni, and Audio Flamingo 3. GPT-4o-Realtime, Step-Audio-Chat, Qwen2-Audio-Chat, VITA-1.5, Llama-Omni, and Mini-Omni leave the QA comparisons. MiniCPM-o 2.6 loses its S→T comparison entries and is removed from the speech-quality table, although its S→S QA results remain.

E3.justification: The grouping study expands factors 1/5 to 1/3/5/7 and replaces the T2M+T2T generation condition with S2M+T2T (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 4). V2 adds GPU-hour comparisons across two backbone sizes with the continuous encoder enabled or disabled. QA averages now cover two benchmarks rather than four or three. Removed scoring-framework documentation does not establish that the underlying scoring procedure changed.

E4.justification: V2 replaces the contrastive-alignment ablation with a continuous-encoder ablation, revises grouping sensitivity, and adds computational-cost analysis. Pretraining analysis already existed in v1 Appendix B/Table 8; v2 incorporates it into Table 5, adds CoM outcomes, and changes the comparison control. Several other ablation rows and Figure 3's data-scaling curves are retained. The duplex analysis is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Both present point estimates and scaling/sensitivity plots without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The main model's Llama Questions S→T/S→S entries change from 79.7/65.0 to 85.0/71.0, and Web Questions from 51.7/30.0 to 65.2/40.1 (v1 Tables 2–3; v2 Table 2). These are revised reported results, not established same-setting gains, given the model changes and reduced protocol disclosure. Baseline entries also change, including Moshi's Llama Questions S→S score from 43.7 to 21.0. Encoder/grouping/cost results are added, while speech-quality scores and data-scaling curves are retained.

T1.justification: V1's negative-cosine alignment definition is removed, and its three-term training objective becomes a two-term objective (v1 Equations 4 and 8; v2 Equation 7). V2 also revises the written speech-loss conditioning from H to H<i and text-loss conditioning from t<i to c<i. These are limited mathematical-definition revisions; neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The contribution framing shifts from dual resolution plus contrastive alignment and demonstrated duplex capability to dual-resolution efficiency and a claimed CoM-Mixing curriculum. The abstract and conclusion broaden the performance claim from SOTA among parallel models to SOTA among similarly sized speech foundation models, adding stronger efficiency and small-data claims. Full-duplex capability becomes future work.

C2.justification: V1 interprets grouping as helping understanding but harming T2M generation; v2 interprets its different S2M experiment as showing benefits to both generation and efficiency. The contrastive objective's speech-versus-text tradeoff discussion disappears, replaced by an encoder-based explanation of improved speech understanding. CoM receives a stronger reasoning/curriculum interpretation, and full-duplex interaction becomes an unimplemented direction. The tokenization-related speech-quality limitation remains.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the continuous encoder, adapter functions, and SIL padding, and changes reported hardware from 32 A100 GPUs to 32 A800 GPUs and post-training time from approximately 20 to 45 hours. It removes v1's evaluation-framework access information, judge versions and scoring templates, and reduced-training qualification for the pretraining ablation. The promised code release remains, but its named repository destination is omitted.

R1.justification: The contrastive-alignment related-work subsection and its CLIP, VILA-U, and speech-contrastive references are removed. V2 adds discussion/references for newer systems including VITA-Audio, LLaMA-Omni2, and Stream-Omni. Positioning relative to Kimi-Audio changes substantively: v1 contrasts its discrete-token alignment approach with Kimi's continuous features, whereas v2 adopts an inspired continuous encoder and emphasizes its lower frame rate.

P1.justification: Beyond model/component renaming, the abstract, contribution narrative, related work, methodology overview, and results discussion are extensively rewritten. The separate SRM section is incorporated into the MLLM section, interaction-pattern training is reframed as CoM-Mixing, and scaling analysis moves into the main discussion. Three substantive appendices become a single prompt-template appendix.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn to show the continuous encoder, adapter, tokenizer/detokenizer, and generation heads. Separate S→T/S→S benchmark tables are merged with frame-rate columns and model-size groupings; ablation tables are reorganized. V2 adds the GPU-cost chart, relocates the retained scaling plot, and removes the duplex diagram/table and evaluation-template panels.

improvement.justification: V2's encoder ablation, grouping-factor sweep, GPU-cost evidence, and newer comparators strengthen support for the revised architecture. However, broader SOTA claims accompany narrower QA coverage and removal of reproducible scoring details. Table 5 retains v1's no-pretraining results without its reduced-training qualification, leaving control comparability unresolved. Table 2 also lists a Qwen2.5-Omni average of 74.1 despite component scores of 75.3 and 62.8. These benefits coexist with weaker traceability and comparison inconsistencies, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
